entries.reason: the class is a circle and nothing else: a centre, a radius, the diameter that is twice it, and the two membership tests the header declares. That is arithmetic over a VNPoint and a double, so the class is here in full
entries.effect: a VNCircle built with -initWithCenter:radius: or -initWithCenter:diameter: answers center, radius and diameter; -containsPoint: answers YES for a point on the boundary as well as inside, and -containsPoint:inCircumferentialRingOfWidth: answers YES for a point in the band of the given width about the boundary, which is the band the header describes as radius-delta to radius+delta with the width the argument names

entries.reason: the class is one computation over a set of points: the smallest circle that holds them. It is found by the three cases its own name implies - a point on its own, two as a diameter, three as the circle through them - over the points shuffled by a constant-seeded generator, so the same points answer the same circle on every run
entries.effect: +boundingCircleForPoints:error: and +boundingCircleForSIMDPoints:pointCount:error: answer the smallest VNCircle holding every point given, and a point outside the circle is never the answer; no points, or a nil among them, answers nil with VNErrorInvalidArgument. The two contour overloads, +calculateArea:forContour:orientedArea:error: and +calculatePerimeter:forContour:error:, are NOT declared, because both take a VNContour and that class's row in this file is absent: respondsToSelector: answers honestly and an unchecked call raises

entries.reason: the class is a point and nothing else: two coordinates, the distance between two of them, and a vector applied to one. Every part of that is a double, so it is here in full - the origin is the zero point, a vector translates, and a point copies and archives as NSSecureCoding, which its own header declares
entries.effect: a VNPoint built with -initWithX:y: or -initWithLocation: answers x, y and location, -distanceToPoint: answers the Euclidean distance, +pointByApplyingVector:toPoint: translates and +distanceBetweenPoint:point: asks two points, and -copyWithZone: and -initWithCoder: round trip it; no argument of nil is a distance and answers NaN, and zeroPoint is the origin
